key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation in metal halide perovskites from early time-series data, enabling faster stability prediction for unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical screening tool for perovskite solar-cell materials by reducing the time and experimental cost needed to assess stability under heat and light stress.
method: Collected 167 perovskite samples spanning diverse compositions and crystallinities.
Stressed samples with elevated temperature and illumination while monitoring photoluminescence over time.
Featurized more than 86,000 PL spectra with a physics-informed model and trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM forecaster.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on samples unseen during training and outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Forecast quality may depend on how well the training dataset covers new compositions, crystallinities, and stress conditions encountered in deployment.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
